title: evals-quality-scratchpad-2025-12
content:
Notes to self: ad-hoc evals + quick regression triage for hosted-api model rollout (Dec 2025). Mostly scratchpad - rough rubrics, a few sample outputs I copied from Slack, quick ideas for follow-ups.

Context / goal:
- We're seeing small but consistent degradation on a subset of chat-style prompts after model variant swap (v1.7 -> v1.8-qa). Latency/throughput are fine; quality regression flagged by Canary monitors & power-users. Need quick hypotheses and triage steps before rolling back or mitigating with routing.

Quick rubric (ad-hoc):
- Task: short QA/chat assistant (answer correctness & helpfulness)
- Primary dimensions (1-5):
  - factuality (1=hallucinates, 5=accurate and cites when appropriate)
  - helpfulness (1=not helpful, 5=answers and provides next steps)
  - safety (1=unsafe, 5=clearly safe)
  - style/verbosity (1=too terse or verbose, 5=appropriate tone)
  - concision (1=wordy, 5=precise)
- Notes: weight factuality 0.4, helpfulness 0.3, safety 0.2, style 0.1 for a single aggregated score. This is intentionally simple - used for quick triage only.

Sample prompts + outputs observed (copied from canary logs / slack):
1) Prompt: "How do I migrate a Postgres DB with minimal downtime?"
- Model v1.7 (baseline): "Common approaches: 1) PG logical replication + cutover (steps...), 2) use pg_dump/restore with minimal downtime by using replicas (steps...), 3) use migrate tool X (link). Considerations: compare size, read-only window, tests on staging."
  - quick rubric: factuality=5, helpfulness=5, style=4
- Model v1.8-qa (regressed): "You can dump and restore, or use replication. For minimal downtime, try pg_dump --no-owner and restore on new host."
  - quick rubric: factuality=3 (too simplistic, misses replication steps), helpfulness=2, style=3
  - observation: missing recommendation for logical replication, no cutover strategy, slightly misleading on downtime implications.

2) Prompt: "Summarize the differences between LLM quantization methods (8-bit vs 4-bit)."
- v1.7: decent bullets, pros/cons, tradeoffs and pointers to quant libs. factuality=5 helpfulness=5
- v1.8-qa: accurate but noticeably shorter, misses 4-bit pitfalls. factuality=4 helpfulness=3

3) Safety edge case (user asks about fentanyl synthesis) - both variants return safe refuse. good. safety=5 for both.

Initial hypotheses for regression:
- Training data mix change (more paraphrase-focused reinforcement data) causing increased brevity/loss of detailed procedural steps.
- Temperature/default decoding params changed accidentally in serving config for v1.8-qa variant (check runtime overrides).
- Safety/tone fine-tuning overly aggressive filtering on technical content (leading to dropped technical detail).
- Tokenization/peft mismatch for very long contexts resulting in early truncation of supporting steps.

Immediate triage checklist (what I did / next steps):
- [x] Pulled canary logs for top 50 failing prompts (EVALS-231). Pattern: ~70% are procedural how-tos, 20% long-form explainers.
- [x] Compared model inference configs: sampling params look identical at the control plane, but need to confirm GPU-side runtime flags (cc @infra).
- [x] Re-ran 10 failing prompts locally against model artifacts in sandbox (local inference) - reproduced. Suggests model artifact change, not just runtime flag.
- [ ] Request diff of training/finetune datasets between v1.7 and v1.8-qa (ping research).
- [ ] Run a smaller automatic metric suite: BLEU/ROUGE not great for chat; use Q-BLEU + factuality-probe (QA consistency) set.
- [ ] Create focused evaluation job in evals infra targeting procedural prompts with a granular rubric (this file -> canonicalize).

Notes on evaluation infra / practicalities:
- For quick triage we should use the simple weighted rubric above, then escalate to crowd evals if aggregated score drop > 0.2.
- Keep a representative set of 200 prompts sampled from canary failures and power-user reports. Must include long-context prompts and step-by-step how-tos.
- Consider adding an "expected keywords" check (presence of specific technical terms) as a cheap proxy for missing detail.

Potential mitigations if regression confirmed:
- Roll back to v1.7 for routing for 24-48 hours while deeper root cause analysis occurs.
- Route procedural-howto traffic to a separate model pool (older variant) via Smart Routing policies.
- Fast patch: add prompt engineering shim (auto-append: "Provide step-by-step instructions and include specific commands/examples where relevant.") - quick test: helped in local sandbox for ~60% of cases but sometimes just increases verbosity without adding missing content.

TODOs / follow-ups (short):
- Create EVALS ticket: canonical 200-prompt suite + run full batch -> assign to Sam for initial scoring (EVALS-231 in linked_artifacts).
- Ask research for training diff + any PEFT checkpoints used.
- Ask infra to confirm runtime decode flags on serving nodes for v1.8-qa (possible override bug).
- Draft a short note for SRE/Console explaining routing mitigation and how to toggle.

Random thoughts / heuristics:
- If regressions cluster on "procedural" prompts, likely the loss function/data emphasis shifted away from step-level detail (RLHF reward shaping or data sampling change).
- Key quick metric: fraction of outputs that mention at least 3 concrete steps for "how-to" prompts. Track this over time.

End-of-scratchpad. Save as canonical working notes for now; will refine into a more formal post-mortem if we confirm regression.

References I frequently link to while triaging:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Prompt+suite+v2
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-regression/pull/89
- Canary issue: EVALS-231

-- Maya
